matched: pkg/metrics/window.go:38 correctness (reported: Index out of bounds on percentile calculation)

findings.title: Index out of bounds on percentile calculation
findings.body: When p is 100.0, the computed index equals `len(sorted)`, which causes an index out of bounds panic when accessing `sorted[idx]`. Additionally, calling Percentile on an empty window will panic. Clamp the index or adjust the calculation to `int(float64(len(sorted)-1) * p / 100.0)` and add a guard for empty windows.

fixtures.name: unclosed rows plus SQL injection
matched: internal/orders/repo.go:36 resource (reported: Unclosed sql.Rows leads to connection leak)
internal/orders/repo.go:35 security (reported: SQL injection via fmt.Sprintf in query construction)

findings.title: SQL injection via fmt.Sprintf in query construction
findings.body: Formatting the 'state' parameter directly into the SQL string via fmt.Sprintf allows SQL injection. Use parameterized queries instead: r.db.QueryContext(ctx, `SELECT id, user_id, total, state FROM orders WHERE user_id = $1 AND state = $2`, userID, state).

findings.title: Unclosed sql.Rows leads to connection leak
findings.body: The rows object returned by QueryContext is never closed. Add 'defer rows.Close()' immediately after checking for errors from QueryContext to prevent database connection leaks.

fixtures.name: concurrent map write race
matched: internal/warm/warm.go:36 concurrency (reported: Concurrent map write race on w.values)
internal/warm/warm.go:33 concurrency (reported: Data race on shared error variable firstErr)

findings.title: Concurrent map write race on w.values
findings.body: Multiple goroutines spawned in the loop concurrently write to w.values[key] without synchronization. Go maps are not safe for concurrent writes and will race or panic. Protect map access with a sync.Mutex or sync.RWMutex.

findings.title: Data race on shared error variable firstErr
findings.body: Multiple goroutines can assign to firstErr concurrently when fetches fail without synchronization. Protect writes to firstErr using a mutex or an atomic mechanism.

fixtures.name: discarded error leading to nil dereference
matched: internal/billing/invoice.go:47 correctness (reported: Discarded error and missing nil check causes panic)

findings.title: Discarded error and missing nil check causes panic
findings.body: On line 47, the error from s.store.Customer is discarded, and on line 48, fields are accessed on `c` without checking if `c` is nil or if `err` occurred. This will result in a nil pointer dereference panic if a customer is not found. Check `err` and verify `c != nil` before accessing `c.Plan`.

fixtures.name: read-modify-write lost update
matched: internal/wallet/wallet.go:24 data-integrity (reported: Read-modify-write race condition causes lost updates)

findings.title: Read-modify-write race condition causes lost updates
findings.body: Reading the balance on line 24 and updating it on line 31 outside of a transaction or atomic update allows concurrent calls to overwrite each other's changes. Instead, perform the debit atomically in SQL (e.g., UPDATE wallets SET balance_cents = balance_cents - $1 WHERE user_id = $2 AND balance_cents >= $1) or wrap the check-and-update in a database transaction with a row lock.
